title: Energy Markets - France (CDD)
description:
About Us

At Axle Energy, we’re building the infrastructure that will underpin the decarbonised energy system. Our software moves energy usage to times when electricity is cheap and green, by controlling vehicle charging, heating systems, inverters and home batteries. We control hundreds of thousands of energy assets.

We’re building in a legacy industry and moving gigawatt-hours of electrons in the real world, but we operate at lightning speed, and we’re growing the team to meet customer demand.

We’re proud to be supported by world-leading investors, including Energize Capital and Accel. Read more about what we’re building here .

France is one of the most important flexibility markets in Europe. This role is critical to accelerating Axle’s growth in France.

About the role

Axle has quickly become the leader in our operational markets, and we’re now looking to expand our reach in France.

At the core of our market expansion plans is market analysis. To maximise future revenue, we spend a lot of time understanding the value of flexibility in power markets around the world.

We are looking for a technical individual (data scientist, analyst or engineer) with strong knowledge of the French electricity markets and an instinct for commercial value.

You will become Axle’s internal expert on French power markets: understanding the market rules, modelling the value, and building relationships with system operators and regulators. We’re scrappy about method and rigorous about conclusions.

You will speak fluent French and English. Other European languages will also be an asset.

What you will be doing

- Developing a deep understanding of French energy markets and grid dynamics to understand how trading, compensation, penalties and cash flow work

- Jumping on the phone with grid operators, regulators and market stakeholders to validate hypotheses and make sense of data

- Building and optimising models of wholesale/NEBCO, capacity, balancing, ancillary services and local flexibility markets in France to forecast what different assets can earn

- Sizing the revenue opportunity across markets and products to shape where we expand next

- Building and evaluating different strategies for cycling a battery or load-shifting an EV charger

- Monitoring and shaping energy regulation to accelerate the growth of flexibility.

This is an opportunity to gain unique domain expertise and build the quantitative case for first-of-a-kind projects across the world.

What we think you need to be successful

- Deep quantitative and modelling ability (Python, SQL)

- Exceptional communication and the ability to turn data into actionable commercial insights

- Comfort moving fast and making decisions in an evolving environment

- Deep knowledge of French electricity markets (NEBCO, Mécanisme de Capacité, Mécanisme d’Ajustement, ancillary services…)

- Relationships with regulators, grid operators and other stakeholders (CRE, DGEC, RTE, Enedis, etc.) are a plus

What’s in it for you

This is a 12 month fixed-term contract (CDD). Compensation is highly competitive and dependent on experience.

We operate with a deliberately flat structure and aim to keep pay equitable across the company, with a 1:1 median ratio between founder and team compensation.

Bi-annual retreats to strengthen team connection & shared purpose.

You’ll be based in France. To maximise collaboration, we ask that you spend ~1 week per month working from our London office.

The opportunity to directly shape the future of energy markets and accelerate the transition to a low-carbon world.

We are extremely keen to build a diverse team, and we’re particularly eager to hear from candidates who don't fit the traditional role stereotypes. If you’re motivated by our mission, please do reach out, even if you feel you might not ‘check all the boxes’.

Interview process

- Initial interview

- Take-home exercise

- Final interview (in-person)

- Offer, references, and welcome to the team!

TES RESPONSABILITÉS

- Définir et faire évoluer le cadre de Data Governance :

- Unified Trust & DQ Metrics Store : Participer à la structuration du Data Quality Metrics Store pour offrir une vision unifiée et transparente de la santé des données.

- Data Knowledge & Context Layer : Structurer la connaissance technico-fonctionnelle dans le catalogue de données (Collibra) et promouvoir la couche de contexte ( Context Layer ) pour faciliter la découvrabilité et le lignage des données.

- Shift-Left & Remédiation : Déployer le modèle de responsabilité partagée avec les producteurs de données ( Quality by Design ) et standardiser le suivi des plans de remédiation.

- Soutenir une Digital Unit / Domaine :

- Accompagner la pratique fonctionnelle et technique du Data Stewardship au sein d'une verticale dédiée.

- Réaliser des formations techniques et méthodologiques auprès des Data Stewards, Data Owners et producteurs.

- Évaluer la maturité Data Governance du domaine et accompagner les trajectoires vers la certification des actifs critiques.

- Apporter un support au quotidien et participer au recrutement des futurs coéquipiers.

- Contribuer à définir les standards d'excellence métier et évaluer le niveau d'expertise lors des recrutements de la filière Data Governance au sein des domaines.

CE QUE TU APPORTES 

- Leadership & Influence : Tu cultives des relations solides et basées sur la confiance avec un large éventail d'interlocuteurs internes et externes, en gérant de manière experte les attentes et en favorisant l'alignement sur les objectifs stratégiques. Tu fais preuve d'une forte capacité d'influence sans autorité directe, navigues efficacement dans les dynamiques organisationnelles et géres ta hiérarchie de manière proactive. Tu escalades les enjeux critiques de façon stratégique et en garantis la résolution.

- Rigueur & Analyse : Capacité à documenter, structurer des règles et résoudre des problèmes complexes

- Métier & Gouvernance : Les concepts de Data Governance, Data Quality Management, Data Lineage et Data Knowledge ne te sont pas inconnus

- Solide Compréhension Technique :

- Tu sais analyser, requêter et manipuler la donnée (langage SQL a minima).

- Tu comprends les grands principes d’architectures Data modernes (Data Lake, Data Products, Data Contracts,...).

- Tu as une connaissance des outils de Data Quality et de Data cataloging.

- Capacité d'articulation Tech & Business : Tu sais traduire des besoins métier complexes en exigences techniques de gouvernance et vice-versa.

STACK TECHNIQUE 

Dans ton quotidien, tu évolueras au sein d'un écosystème technologique moderne incluant :

- Gouvernance & Métadonnées : Collibra, Unity Catalog

- Data Architecture & Transformation : Databricks, DBT, Airflow, Python

QUALIFICATIONS 

- Diplôme (Licence, Master ou École d'Ingénieur) en Informatique, Data, Systèmes d'Information ou domaine connexe.

- 1-3 ans d'expérience au minimum en Data Governance, Data Stewardship, Data Quality ou gestion de programme data.

- Expérience probante dans l'animation de communautés et la conduite du changement.

- Anglais courant (niveau B2/C1 minimum) dans un environnement international.

CE QUE NOUS T’OFFRONS 

Organisation de travail hybride ;

Matériel fourni en accord avec tes missions et nos engagements sociétaux (Mac ou Windows) ;

Une équipe de projet locale au sein d'un réseau mondial (possibilité de carrière internationale) ;

Développement des compétences et accompagnement (diversité des projets, formations internes et externes, etc.) ;

Package de rémunération (actionnariat salarié, bonus mensuels/trimestriels).

NOTRE ENGAGEMENT EN FAVEUR DE L'INCLUSION ET DE L'ACCESSIBILITE

title: Alliance & Delivery Manager, Pharma Partnerships
description:
About Orakl Oncology

At Orakl Oncology, we combine patient-derived tumor models, experimental drug screening and computational modelling to improve oncology drug development. Our research brings together functional treatment-response measurements, molecular profiles and clinical information where available, creating opportunities to investigate how experimental responses translate into patient outcomes. Our platforms are designed to help anticipate clinical trial outcomes, evaluate therapies and identify new therapeutic opportunities.

Our mission is simple yet ambitious: to bring more effective treatments to patients who need them and to make drug development smarter, faster, and more personalised. We collaborate with top hospitals, research institutes, and pharmaceutical companies worldwide. Backed by leading investors, we are a fast-growing, mission-driven startup at the intersection of science and technology.

About the Role

We are looking for an Alliance & Delivery Manager to own Orakl's pharma partnerships after signature: the partner relationship, the delivery of each research program, and the growth of each account.

Orakl runs research programs for pharmaceutical companies on its virtual patient cohorts, combining compound screening, multi-omics and O-Predict analyses on the partner's assets. Several programs run in parallel on the same wet-lab and dry-lab teams, and the portfolio is growing. Delivery quality directly drives renewals and follow-on contracts.

This is a high-ownership, partner-facing role . You are the partner's main contact, you are accountable for delivery across our wet-lab and dry-lab teams, and you grow existing accounts. You will also scale our delivery processes and tooling: project tracking, capacity planning and partner reporting, automated wherever possible.

You will work closely with the Scientific Program & Operations Lead, Business Development, the Wet Lab, Data Science and Computational Biology leads, and Product. As the ideal candidate, you have already delivered complex scientific programs for pharma clients, and you are an expert at establishing partner trust.

What You'll Do

Own partner relationships: act as the main point of contact for each pharma partner from kick-off to final delivery. Map decision-makers, priorities and expectations for their asset, run the steering committees, attend key international conferences a few times per year and present results alongside our scientific teams.

Lead program delivery: translate each signed contract into an executable plan for the Wet Lab and Dry Lab teams, with owners, milestones and deliverables. Own the timeline, coordinate the experimental and computational work, and ensure every deliverable passes internal QC and review before it reaches the partner.

Manage capacity across programs: plan capacity with the Wet Lab and Dry Lab leads, arbitrate conflicts between programs and protect committed timelines. Centralise requests on delivery teams coming from partners and Business Development.

Manage risk and change: anticipate delivery risks, including results that change the plan, and escalate to the Scientific Program & Operations Lead with a recommendation. Agree and document scope and timeline changes with partners.

Scale delivery processes and tooling: scale our project management system in Asana, from program templates and timelines to portfolio and capacity views. Automate reporting and follow-up, deploy AI tools where they remove manual work, and document how we run programs.

Grow existing accounts: identify, qualify and convert follow-on opportunities within existing partnerships. Work with Business Development on scoping, proposals and pricing, and provide a feasibility assessment before anything is committed.

Plan scientific and BD materials: schedule conference and BD material cycles as part of the delivery plan, and coordinate partner approvals for any communication based on partnered programs.

Minimum Qualifications

- 4+ years in project management, alliance and/or account management, or partner delivery in biotech, pharma, a CRO or a techbio.

- Master's degree in a scientific or engineering field. A PhD is a strong plus.

- Demonstrated delivery of complex scientific programs: you have led multidisciplinary projects from plan to final deliverable, including when results reshaped the plan.

- Pharma-facing experience: you have managed pharma stakeholders through steering committees, negative results and scope negotiations.

- Commercial track record: you have identified and converted follow-on opportunities within existing accounts.

- Hands-on systems building: you have designed project management systems and automated recurring workflows.

- Working knowledge of oncology or molecular biology, sufficient to lead scientific discussions with our teams and partners.

- Fluent in English

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience in precision oncology or at a pharma-facing CRO.

- Familiarity with patient-derived tumor models, omics or drug screening.

- Scripting (Python) or experience deploying automation and AI tools.

- Experience working with SOWs and contracts.

- Professional French.

Who You Are

- An owner: you take responsibility for outcomes across teams you do not manage, and you make explicit trade-offs when programs compete.

- Scientifically fluent: you understand what a result means for the partner's asset before you plan around it.

- Steady under pressure: you replan quickly if the data changes, and you deliver difficult news to partners clearly and early.

- A builder: you treat every recurring manual task as something to standardise or automate.

- Commercially minded: you recognise when a partner's needs extend beyond the signed scope and turn it into a proposal.

Why Join Orakl

- Own a portfolio of pharma partnerships. Represent Orakl from signature to final delivery, with direct access to partner decision-makers.

- Work on distinctive science. Deliver programs built on virtual patients cohorts, functional drug screening & multi-omics.

- Build the delivery model. Design how Orakl runs partnered programs as the portfolio scales.

- Work across disciplines every day. Alongside the biologists, data scientists and computational biologists who generate the results.

- Help shape the team. Define the delivery capabilities and future team needs as the partnership portfolio grows.

Interview Process

- Hiring Manager Call: align on motivation, role scope and expectations.

- Technical Deep Dive: discuss a pharma program you delivered: the plan, the problems, how you managed the partner and the outcome.

- Delivery Case: using an anonymised, representative scenario, build a plan, triage issues and prepare a steering committee. Present it to the team.

- Reference Call: speak with one or two people who have seen you manage partners and deliver programs.

- Founder Interview: discuss Orakl's partnership strategy and mutual ambitions.

title: Security Engineer
description:
WHO WE ARE 

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

WHY JOIN US 

- Work on a civilisation-scale problem - Clean, baseload fusion energy is one of the few genuinely world-changing challenges, and every hire directly accelerates the path to a working stellarator.

- Grow as fast as the company does - With headcount set to roughly 5x in a few years and major technical milestones ahead on the path to our demo machine and first power plant, your role grows under you; today's hire is tomorrow's function lead.

- Tackle problems that don't exist elsewhere - Fusion sits at a rare intersection of deep-tech R&D, industrial procurement, government relations, and venture financing, so non-tech functions face challenges no other workplace can offer.

YOUR IMPACT

As our Senior Security Engineer in Munich, you will own security implementation and security monitoring, digital and physical, for a company building one of the most valuable bodies of fusion IP in Europe. Protecting it is its own challenge, and you are the person who will own it.

WHAT YOU WILL DO 

• Build out our security monitoring capability: select and run the SIEM, decide what's worth alerting on, and tune out the noise.

• Own incident response end-to-end, from investigation through to a post-mortem and a fix that holds.

• Harden the environment hands-on across endpoint and EDR, identity and access, network, and infrastructure.

• Finish maturing Zero Trust: identity and device posture as joint conditions for access, and MFA everywhere.

• Handle the long tail of edge cases that comes with a fast-growing team and a lot of contractors.

• Secure our Google-centric workplace, where most of our IP moves — DLP, data classification and labeling, retention, and context-aware access.

• Secure the software supply chain in collaboration with our platform team: source control, access boundaries, secrets, and CI/CD.

• Run vulnerability and attack surface management, and drive remediation to be done with the teams that own the systems.

• Set and monitor our physical security standard with Business Operations, who implement it on site: access zones, CCTV and alerting, visitor and contractor access, and site access as one joiner-mover-leaver process with digital access, across multiple locations.

• Give our compliance work the technical substance it needs: evidence, remediation, and support through audits and pen tests.

WHO YOU ARE 

Must have 

• You have 5+ years hands-on in security engineering, with real depth in identity, endpoint, and infrastructure.

• You have built or substantially operated a SIEM, and run real incidents end-to-end.

• You have implemented Zero Trust in production - unified IdP and MDM, conditional access, device posture.

• You know Google Workspace Enterprise security well, or can get there fast from an equivalent platform.

• You are automation-first: Terraform, and scripting in Python, Bash, or PowerShell are no strangers to you.

• You are fluent in CIS Benchmarks, NIST, ISO 27001, and NIS2 without being ruled by them.

• You can turn a technical finding into a business impact and actionable solutions

Nice to have 

• Interest or a track record in AI security.

• Hands-on cloud and container security: GCP, containers, Kubernetes.

• Certifications such as CISSP, GCIA, GCIH, CCSP, or Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer.

• Experience in a regulated, export-controlled, or high-security environment, where physical and digital security meet.

INTERVIEW PROCESS 

- Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

title: Quantum Applications Engineer
description:
Quandela is a global leader in quantum computing, designing, building, and delivering cutting-edge quantum solutions for research and industry. Its offerings include very energy-efficient quantum computers for data centers, full-stack quantum computing solutions accessible via the cloud, and algorithm access services for academic and industrial customers. Following a pragmatic, step-by-step roadmap, Quandela has been deploying industrial-grade systems since 2023 while developing future generations of fault-tolerant quantum computers capable of scaling through the integration of thousands of photonic components. Quandela is committed to making quantum computing accessible to all in order to address the most complex industrial and societal challenges. Learn more at: Quandela | Leading Photonic Quantum Computing Solutions 

Description of the Project 

As a Quantum Applications Engineer , you will work at the intersection of quantum algorithms, real-world applications and customer projects .

Your mission will be to identify relevant problems that can be addressed using Quandela's quantum computing technology, assess their feasibility and define how meaningful performance should be measured.

Working directly with industrial and academic partners, you will translate real-world challenges into quantum computing problems, evaluate potential approaches and establish the appropriate benchmarks against classical methods.

This is a highly technical role with strong exposure to customers and partners. It is particularly suited to someone with a background in quantum algorithms who wants to apply that expertise to practical use cases rather than focus exclusively on theoretical research.

Your Key Responsibilities 

- Identify and assess quantum use cases by working with customers, industrial partners and internal teams to understand their challenges and translate them into relevant computational problems.
- Perform feasibility studies to determine whether and how these problems can be addressed using current and near-term quantum computing technologies, with a particular focus on NISQ approaches.
- Define meaningful benchmarks , including relevant problem instances, expected outputs, accuracy targets and classical baselines to objectively evaluate quantum approaches.
- Explore promising application domains and contribute to application roadmaps, from near-term demonstrations to longer-term utility-scale applications.
- Evaluate scientific, industrial and economic value to help prioritize the applications where quantum computing can have the greatest impact.
- Design and maintain strategic demonstrations and Proofs of Concept , working with internal teams or external software partners depending on the project.
- Follow customer projects throughout their lifecycle , including projects where algorithm development is performed by external partners.
- Present technical work to customers and partners , explaining quantum approaches, results, limitations and opportunities to both technical and non-specialist audiences.
- Collaborate closely with Quandela's algorithm, machine learning, product, project management, sales and engineering teams.
Depending on the strategic interest of a project, you may also contribute directly to the development and implementation of quantum algorithms in Python.

What will make you successful

You do not need to know every possible quantum application from day one.

What matters is your ability to approach an unfamiliar problem, ask the right questions, understand its computational structure and determine whether quantum computing provides an interesting direction to explore.

You are comfortable navigating between research and practical applications : scientifically rigorous enough to challenge an algorithmic approach, pragmatic enough to assess its real-world relevance, and comfortable enough with people to discuss your conclusions directly with customers.

Requirements 

You have a strong technical background in quantum computing and quantum algorithms , combined with the curiosity and communication skills required to explore real-world applications.

You ideally bring:

- A PhD in quantum computing, quantum information, physics, applied mathematics, computer science or a related field , or a Master's degree combined with relevant professional experience.
- A first professional experience in a similar environment is strongly preferred.
- Strong understanding of quantum algorithms , particularly approaches applicable to current or near-term quantum computers.
- Knowledge of NISQ algorithms and variational quantum algorithms .
- Good programming skills, particularly in Python .
- The ability to understand a complex industrial or scientific problem and translate it into a computational and algorithmic framework.
- A rigorous approach to benchmarking quantum and classical methods .
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Excellent communication skills and the confidence to present technical topics directly to customers, partners and broader audiences.
- Professional proficiency in English .
Previous experience working on customer-facing technical projects, quantum application projects, consulting, pre-sales, collaborative R&D projects or industrial partnerships would be a strong plus.

Experience with Agile ways of working and tools such as Jira is appreciated but not essential.

Benefits 

- Competitive salary, flexible based on your experience 
- Profit-sharing & company savings plan
- 100% health coverage (Alan)
- 50% transport reimbursement or sustainable mobility bonus
- Meal vouchers (Swile), Gymlib fitness support
- Childcare assistance & referral bonuses (€1,000–€2,000)

What we offer: 

- A role at the intersection of cutting-edge quantum research and real-world industrial applications.
- Direct exposure to a wide variety of quantum computing use cases and industries.
- The opportunity to work with leading researchers, engineers, industrial partners and customers.
- Significant ownership in shaping Quandela's application portfolio and identifying the problems quantum computing should address next.
- The opportunity to work across the full quantum stack, from algorithms and software to Quandela's photonic quantum computing technology.
- A hybrid work model (3-4 days/week onsite in Massy, 1 day in Paris or 1 to 2 days remotely).

- Meeting with the teams

title: Technical Business Development Intern (Emerging Verticals) (f/m/d)
description:
Description 

QuantumDiamonds is building the world's first commercial quantum sensing tools for chip failure analysis. Our Quantum Diamond Microscope (QDm) images magnetic fields with micrometer resolution, and that capability could matter far beyond semiconductors. As our Technical Business Development Intern for Emerging Verticals in the Data Science & Machine Learning team in Pre-Development, you help us find out where.

Working directly with our project lead for Emerging Verticals, who mentors you, you explore new application fields for widefield magnetic imaging. You dig into the science and the markets behind them, talk to potential customers and users, and help turn promising ideas into first feasibility studies with our magnetic field imaging system. You see how a deep tech company decides where its technology goes next, and help shape that decision.

This is a full-time internship for 6 months, starting as soon as possible.

Who we are 

Founded in 2022 as a spin-off of TU Munich, QD leverages quantum sensors to rapidly capture three-dimensional current maps within multi-layer chips. Our strong, international team of over 70, including physicists, engineers, data scientists, and other experts, works side by side with major semiconductor manufacturers, supporting chip debugging and accelerating yield analysis. Backed by top-tier deep tech investors, semiconductor experts, and strategic public programs, we have ensured long-term stability, shifting from breakthrough to scale - and shaping the next chapter in chip testing.

Why join Quantum Diamonds? 

Picture this: 

- Quantum sensors that see inside the most advanced chips on Earth, right where two frontier fields collide.

- Nobel-Prize physics aimed at real customers with real problems, in production now, not someday.

- Physicists, data scientists, and engineers building side by side, turning deep science into tools the industry actually runs on.

- An international team that runs at hard problems for fun, where knowledge moves fast and so do you.

Still unsure about why joining us? 

- You'll get to build a company together with a brilliant and welcoming team on a product that has never been done before.

- From Day 1, you'll own your own topics end to end and see the direct impact of your work on how the world sees QuantumDiamonds.

- Our technology is the cutting edge of tomorrow, starting today and not in 10 years.

- You’ll be part of a high-growth company backed by top-tier investors.

Let’s make the invisible visible! 

What will you do 

- Map and evaluate application areas for magnetic field imaging beyond semiconductors: key players, customer segments and structured comparisons of use cases.

- Review scientific literature and patents to understand the state of the art, competing measurement methods, and where NV-based imaging offers a real advantage.

- Prepare and join discovery conversations with researchers and companies to understand their measurement challenges, and keep contacts and opportunities up to date in our CRM.

- Support feasibility studies with our experts, from defining suitable samples to interpreting first measurement results.

- Turn your findings into clear deliverables such as application one-pagers, decision memos, and presentations.

What is expected of you 

- Enrolled in or recently graduated from a degree program in physics, engineering, materials science, chemistry, biophysics, or a related natural science or engineering field, ideally with some Python exposure.

- Available full time for 6 months, starting as soon as possible.

- Curiosity about how a new measurement technology can solve problems in fields you may not know yet.

- Clear writing and structured analysis: you turn a pile of papers and conversations into a one-page recommendation.

- AI tools are part of how you research, analyze and write, and you check their output the way you check your own.

- Fluent in English. On-site in Munich.

Business studies or first experience in market research, consulting, or a startup is a plus, not required.

Our benefits 

- Mission: At QD, we’re driven by more than just building great products - we aim to make a lasting difference. Joining us means contributing to meaningful work that goes beyond business as usual.

- Impact & growth: This is an exciting stage of our journey, and your voice matters. You’ll have the chance to shape our culture, influence key decisions, and grow alongside a company that’s scaling fast.

- Mentoring: An experienced colleague from the team mentors you throughout your internship.

- Health & fitness: With a company-sponsored Wellpass membership, you’ll have access to countless gyms, classes, and wellness offers across Germany to stay healthy and active.

- Team & culture: We believe the best ideas come when we connect outside the office. From regular off-sites to team events, you’ll be part of a collaborative and supportive environment.

- Well-being & balance: We value rest and recovery. That’s why you’ll enjoy 24 vacation days plus public holidays to recharge and return inspired.

About us 

QuantumDiamonds GmbH, headquartered in Munich, Germany, develops and manufactures semiconductor inspection systems based on quantum sensing. Spun out of the Technical University of Munich in 2022, the company uses nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond to map electrical current with micrometer precision inside advanced 2.5D and 3D chip architectures. Nine of the world's ten largest semiconductor manufacturers are engaged with QuantumDiamonds, with systems deployed across Europe, the United States, and Asia. The company is investing €152 million to build the world's first production facility for quantum sensing-based semiconductor inspection tools, supported under the European Chips Act.

QV.AC is a general purpose AI assistant that runs locally on your devices. It gives people real control over their data and how they use AI. title: Industrial Software Engineer - Railway Applications (m/w/d) 80-100%
description:

We believe that rail transport is a cornerstone of a greener future, and our mission is to make it quieter, more efficient, and more reliable.

Our talented team is at the heart of this mission, and we are looking for an Industrial Software Engineer - Railway Applications to join us in developing robust software solutions that operate reliably in real-world railway environments.

What you will do 

- Industrial Software Development: Design, implement and maintain robust application software for industrial and railway products using C++, C#, Python or comparable technologies.

- Application & System Integration: Translate system and operational requirements into practical software functionality and integrate software with real hardware and physical systems.

- Hardware & Device Interfaces: Integrate sensors, actuators, controllers, DAQ systems and other industrial devices.

- Communication Protocols: Implement and troubleshoot interfaces such as CAN/CANopen, EtherCAT, TCP/IP and other industrial or vehicle communication protocols.

- Controls & Application Logic: Implement state machines, operational logic, control functionality and system behaviour required by the application.

- Commissioning & Field Support: Support installation, commissioning and field testing on prototypes, test systems and rail vehicles, including travel to customer and test sites when required.

- Diagnostics & Troubleshooting: Analyse logs, interfaces and system behaviour to identify root causes and solve software and integration issues efficiently.

- Testing & Validation: Develop unit, integration and system-level tests and contribute to HIL/SIL or other validation activities where relevant.

- Software Architecture, Quality & Controlled Releases: Own software architecture and release discipline, including configuration and version control, code reviews, test evidence and controlled software releases.

- Product Cybersecurity: Own threat assessment, secure access and software updates, vulnerability handling and lifecycle security maintenance; coordinate specialist security reviews and work with Systems/RAMS on vehicle interfaces and safety consequences.

- Technical Guidance & Mentoring: Review implementations, share practical software-engineering practices and mentor colleagues to strengthen consistency, maintainability and technical ownership across the team.

- Tools & Data: Develop tools for configuration, testing, diagnostics, data acquisition and analysis that support engineering and field activities.

- Documentation & Continuous Improvement: Maintain clear software and interface documentation and improve existing code as Traila products mature from development into deployed systems.

What you bring 

- Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Automation, Mechatronics or a related discipline, or equivalent practical technical experience.

- Hands-on professional software-development experience in an industrial, automation, automotive, machinery or comparable technical environment.

- Proven professional railway software experience, including products released and maintained in service.

- Strong practical programming skills in C++, C#, Python or a comparable industrial software stack; you do not need to be an expert in every language listed.

- Experience developing software that interacts with real hardware, devices or physical systems.

- Experience taking software beyond prototypes into tested, maintainable and deployable industrial use.

- Practical railway software lifecycle experience aligned with EN 50716:2023, including requirements traceability, configuration management and verification/validation appropriate to the required software integrity level; relevant EN 50128 / EN 50657 predecessor experience is also valuable.

- Practical embedded or industrial cybersecurity experience, including secure credentials and access, signed software updates and rollback, and handling vulnerabilities in released products.

- Strong debugging and troubleshooting skills across software, communication and hardware interfaces.

- Experience with Git and structured software-development workflows.

- A practical ownership mindset: comfortable working directly with prototypes, test equipment and deployed systems and driving technical problems through to resolution.

- Ability to work effectively across engineering disciplines and communicate technical issues clearly.

- Fluent English; German is a strong advantage.

Nice to have 

- Experience with industrial Linux, embedded Linux, automation or control systems.

- MATLAB/Simulink, HIL/SIL testing, data acquisition or condition-monitoring experience.

- Working knowledge of railway cybersecurity under CLC/TS 50701:2023 and of EN IEC 62443-4-1 (secure development) and EN IEC 62443-4-2 (component security) is desirable.

- Familiarity with EN 50155 and EN 50126 for equipment integration and collaboration with Systems/RAMS.

- Experience in a regulated or safety-relevant product-development environment.

Benefits 

- 25 days of annual leave, plus paid bridge days at Christmas.

- Flexible working hours and home office options.

- Annual professional development allowance for courses, certifications and conferences.

- Competitive compensation with milestone bonus scheme and full Swiss social coverage.

- A collaborative team culture with regular social and sports activities.

- Real autonomy and short decision-making paths.

If you want your software engineering to have real-world impact in rail, we’d like to hear from you. 

Contact Yasi Samari, HR Responsible, by applying directly here.

title: Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention & Investigations
description:
Headquarters: Remote - USA

Clover Health is investing in our fraud detection and investigation capabilities and is seeking a Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention & Investigations to join our Legal department as a senior individual contributor. This hybrid role combines: (1) managing hands-on investigations of potential provider fraud with (2) building AI-powered tools and processes to make investigations more efficient and help catch potential future fraud earlier. You will develop and pilot new AI-enabled investigatory processes for Clover’s Medicare Advantage business, and own resulting investigations, in collaboration with Clover’s Special Investigations Unit (SIU) and other stakeholders.

This is a non-attorney role. You will work hand-in-hand with Clover’s lawyers and SIU to ensure that new investigatory processes you develop, and the resulting investigations, comply with Clover policies and regulatory requirements. Success in this role requires someone sharp, creative, and technically hands-on—someone who does not just use existing analytics tools but builds their own. That might mean writing a script to automate repetitive work, pulling apart a dataset when a standard report falls short, or working with an LLM until it produces something genuinely useful—all with the goal of finding smarter, more effective ways to investigate potential provider fraud.

As a Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention & Investigations, you will: 

- Build Your Own Investigative Tooling: Use AI to write the queries, scripts, and prompts that turn millions of claim lines and/or medical record data into a prioritized list of leads. Prototype detection logic yourself rather than waiting on a roadmap, and hand off what works to data science and engineering to productionize. We expect you to be the person who builds v1.

- Investigate Potential Fraud End-to-End With AI in the Loop: Own a portfolio of fraud investigations sourced using the tooling you develop, in collaboration with Clover’s SIU. Develop investigative plans, gather and analyze evidence (including claims data and medical records), and reach well-supported conclusions. Use LLMs and analytics to compress the parts of an investigation that have always been slow — reading unstructured data, triaging grievance narratives, and sizing exposure. 

- Build Defensible Documentation: Develop case files and memos that are factually complete, well-organized, and prepared with the evidentiary and procedural standards necessary for downstream enforcement, recoveries, or provider actions.

- Collaborate Across Functions: Work with Clover's clinical, compliance, claims, payment integrity, provider relations, revenue operations, and SIU teams to gather information, validate findings, and translate investigative outcomes into operational improvements, provider education, and member impact.

- Communicate Findings Clearly: Prepare concise written reports and oral briefings that translate complex investigative facts into clear narratives for senior leadership and other stakeholders.

Success in this role looks like: 

- In your first 90 days , you have embedded yourself as a trusted partner to both the Legal department and Clover’s SIU. You have built working relationships with key stakeholders across Clover's clinical, compliance, claims, payment integrity, revenue operations, and legal teams, and you have begun working through your initial portfolio of fraud investigations and ad hoc referrals.

- By 6 months , you are independently managing a steady caseload of fraud investigations with consistently high-quality work product, in collaboration with SIU. You have a clear working rhythm with Legal and SIU, and you have built at least one working tool — a script, a notebook, a dashboard, a prompt.

- By 12 months , you have a track record of strong investigations, successful recoveries and/or referrals, and effective cross-functional collaboration. Senior leaders across Clover view you as a trusted person to call when they have a hunch that something doesn't look right and want it examined.

You should get in touch if: 

- Knowledge of healthcare fraud schemes & investigative experience: You have experience in healthcare fraud investigations, program integrity, or SIU operations, ideally within Medicare Advantage or managed care. You understand healthcare fraud schemes and know how to use claims data, medical records, and provider documentation to build a defensible factual record.

- You are AI-native and enjoy building things using LLMs: You can use LLMs to write SQL, Python, etc., to interrogate large claims and/or medical record datasets, automate investigative work, and prototype your own solutions rather than waiting for someone else to build them. We do not expect production-grade engineering or require formal technical training—we value demonstrated ability to build, ship, and showcase solutions that work. 

- Strong communication skills: You are a strong writer and communicator who can turn complex investigative findings into clear memos, referrals, and executive summaries, and you are comfortable building in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment.

Bonus points if: 

- 

- You have built something people actually use—an internal tool, detection model, script, automation, or AI workflow that made a manual process better. We would rather see something scrappy and useful in production than something polished in a slide.

- You have hands-on experience applying AI/ML to fraud, investigations, or compliance.

- You have a J.D., legal training, or experience working alongside Legal, SIU, or compliance at a health plan.

- You have industry certifications such as CFE, AHFI, or CHC.

Benefits Overview :

- Financial Well-Being : Our commitment to attracting and retaining top talent begins with a competitive base salary and equity opportunities. Additionally, we offer a performance-based bonus program, 401k matching, and regular compensation reviews to recognize and reward exceptional contributions.

- Physical Well-Being : We prioritize the health and well-being of our employees and their families by providing comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage. Your health matters to us, and we invest in ensuring you have access to quality healthcare.

- Mental Well-Being : We understand the importance of mental health in fostering productivity and maintaining work-life balance. To support this, we offer initiatives such as No-Meeting Fridays, monthly company holidays, access to mental health resources, and a generous flexible time-off policy. Additionally, we embrace a remote-first culture that supports collaboration and flexibility, allowing our team members to thrive from any location. 

- Professional Development : Developing internal talent is a priority for Clover. We offer learning programs, mentorship, professional development funding, and regular performance feedback and reviews.

Additional Perks: 

- Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offering discounted equity opportunities

- Reimbursement for office setup expenses

- Monthly cell phone & internet stipend

- Remote-first culture, enabling collaboration with global teams

- Paid parental leave for all new parents

- And much more!

About Clover: We are reinventing health insurance by combining the power of data with human empathy to keep our members healthier. We believe the healthcare system is broken, so we've created custom software and analytics to empower our clinical staff to intervene and provide personalized care to the people who need it most.

We always put our members first, and our success as a team is measured by the quality of life of the people we serve. Those who work at Clover are passionate and mission-driven individuals with diverse areas of expertise, working together to solve the most complicated problem in the world: healthcare.

From Clover’s inception, Diversity & Inclusion have always been key to our success. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and our employees are people with different strengths, experiences, perspectives, opinions, and backgrounds, who share a passion for improving people's lives. Diversity not only includes race and gender identity, but also age, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, religion and many other parts of one’s identity. All of our employee’s points of view are key to our success, and inclusion is everyone's responsibility.

title: Manager, Software Engineering, Operations
description:
Want to lead engineers building software that helps pros get the job done and know exactly how their business is doing? 

Then Jobber might be the place for you! We’re looking for a Manager, Software Engineering to be part of our SP (Service Provider) Operations group, focused on helping Service Providers run their day-to-day operations efficiently and effectively.

Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers, while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn’t like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That’s why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want!

Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail’s Canada’s Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada’s Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience of leading the way, we’ve come a long way from our first customer in 2011—but we’ve just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers .

We help employees grow professionally; we have a ton of onboarding resources, tutorials, hackathons and buddies to support learnings and provide opportunities to innovate. We have a range of experience levels on teams which allows for mentor/mentee opportunities. Leaders at Jobber work with empathy and support employees to build healthy work-life harmony. Bring your dedication and passion to this job to fulfill your goals.

The team: 

In this role, you will manage the engineering teams behind one of Jobber's most important domains, Jobs Teams, as part of the greater SP Operations Group. The Jobs Team is at the heart of how service businesses operate, and we are constantly improving how service providers orchestrate work from start to finish so they can confidently deliver every job with quality. You will work alongside peers from Product Management, Design, and the rest of the Engineering Leadership team to ensure the tools we build help small businesses run more efficiently and grow with confidence!

The role: 

As a leader within the SP Operations group, you will manage the engineering teams to deliver high quality, on time while they get to grow and learn along the way. The SP Operations group's mission is to help Service Providers run their businesses as efficiently as possible. We build the tools that help with day-to-day operations, from scheduling and managing work and crew to ensure every job gets done, to giving business owners the visibility they need to understand their business health and make informed decisions.

Reporting to a Senior Manager of Software Engineering, the Manager of Software Engineering will lead and support their team members in developing their skills and advancing their careers—all while contributing to our mission of empowering small businesses. You'll also play a key role in shaping the technical direction of our platform, ensuring it remains reliable and high-performing as we scale Jobber.

The Manager, Software Engineering will: 

- 
Live and breathe performance facilitation. You want to work with your team(s) to help them master their individual crafts, while also collaborating to build extraordinary experiences and systems.

- 
Be committed to the success of your people. You will help them set goals, have regular 1-on-1s, and provide constructive feedback and coaching to ensure your team's success. You’ll work to understand employees’ career direction and work to empower their journey by acting as a mentor and coach.

- 
Develop a world-class team alongside a world-class organization. You’ll participate in recruiting events and the hiring process while also working to level up your internal team while implementing new processes, all to develop a world-class engineering department.

- 
Remove roadblocks and build guardrails. You’ll work with the other leaders to create and maintain an environment where people can rapidly produce top-quality work that ultimately helps our customers be successful.

- 
Collaborate with other stakeholders across the business. Whether it’s our Management teams within Product, or our Business Technology teams, you’re working closely with other Jobberinos to find the best solutions in Jobber for small businesses.

To be successful, you should have: 

- 
A track record of success in being an established software engineer, as well as time spent in a leadership position, guiding a team in the delivery of quality software.

- 
Strong full-stack technical background, including design and architectural experience. 

- 
A drive to succeed and deliver impactful projects on time. For a high performing team with a solid roadmap that might look like getting out of their way, but for a team whose delivery is in doubt, it means getting in and getting dirty, and working with the team to find a path back to success.

- 
The ability to be agile in an agile environment. You’ll need to be able to lead and teach your team to adapt to change, while also thinking critically and creatively to find answers to problems.

- 
Effective written and oral communication. Being transparent with your team and establishing an open dialogue will be a key to success in supporting your coaching conversations and discussions.

- 
To be a leader and mentor. You’ll bring your shared experience into conversations to influence and provide constructive feedback to direct reports throughout the journey to ensure goals are being met and exceeded.

- 
Familiarity or comfort in AI tools and AI augmented development rhythms.

Highly desired, but not a dealbreaker: 

- 
Previous experience with our development stack: ReactJS, Typescript, Ruby on Rails, PostgreSQL, and GraphQL.

- 
Previous experience with building zero to one projects from initial discovery and design, through implementation, and into delivery and measurement.

Location: 

We believe great collaboration is intentional, and sometimes that means coming together in person to build, brainstorm, and connect. To support this, the role is open to candidates based in one of our hub cities: Edmonton, Toronto, Vancouver, or Kitchener-Waterloo.

Compensation: 

At Jobber, we also believe that compensation should be transparent, fair, and supportive of your experience and growth. This role has a minimum annual salary of $169,200 CAD, a midpoint of $199,100 CAD , and a maximum salary of $228,900 CAD, designed to reflect the progression from learning the ropes to truly excelling.

We design our compensation to reflect each new hire's skills, experience, and the complexity of the role, ensuring a fair and competitive salary. Our range is intentionally broad to support growth and long-term impact, with fully established hires typically starting around the midpoint. The higher end of the range is reserved for those who have demonstrated deep expertise and lasting contributions, while offers below the midpoint reflect strong potential with room to develop. This approach ensures that compensation aligns with both an individual's current capabilities and their opportunity for future growth.

Base salary is just one part of a total compensation package that will include equity rewards, annual stipends for health and wellness, retirement savings matching, and an extended health package with fully paid premiums for body and mind. Your professional growth matters to us too! You'll have access to a dedicated talent development program that includes career coaching and opportunities for career development.

We believe in transparency and open conversations about compensation. If you have any questions about our approach, we're happy to discuss them throughout the hiring process!

What you can expect from Jobber: 

- 
A total compensation package that includes an extended health benefits package with fully paid premiums for both body and mind, matching in RRSP, TFSA or FHSA, and stock options.

- 
A dedicated Talent Development team and access to coaching, learning, and leadership programs to help you grow your career, reach your goals, and unlock your full potential.

- 
A unique opportunity to build, grow, and leave your impact on a $400-billion industry that has no dominant player...yet.

- 
To work with a group of people who are humble, supportive, and give a sh*t about our customers.

We believe that diverse teams perform better and that fostering an inclusive work environment is a key part of growing a successful team. We welcome people of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to working with applicants requesting accommodation at any stage of the hiring process. 

A bit more about us: 

Job by job, we’re transforming the way service is delivered. Your lawn care provider, home cleaning service, plumber or painter could use Jobber to better connect with their customers, save time in the office, invoice faster, and get paid! We’re bringing tens of thousands of people together with technology to deliver billions of dollars a year in services to happy customers. Jobber exists to help make these small businesses successful, and when they’re successful we all win!

What You'll Do

- Own the IT and workplace operating and capital budget: forecast it, defend it in planning cycles, and continuously rationalize license, vendor, and facilities spend.

Technology and infrastructure

- Own the endpoint fleet and the SaaS portfolio â Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, IRU, and a long tail of business applications â with enforced MDM baselines for encryption, patching, and configuration.

- Own network and connectivity for the headquarters and the remote workforce, with redundancy appropriate to a company our customers depend on.

- Replace manual provisioning, access reviews, and device setup with scripted, auditable workflows.

title: Software Engineer, Product
description:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. 

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the role

You'll work across LabOS — our internal software platform — building the orchestration layer that coordinates everything from experiment scheduling to execution to data capture and results processing. This is full-stack product engineering at the intersection of software and physical-world biology.

Day-to-day, that can mean things like:

- Creating interfaces and APIs that give scientists and AI agents visibility into what's happening in the lab in real time

- Building custom AI agents and tooling that automate decisions across the experiment lifecycle, from protocol design to troubleshooting failed results

- Turning proprietary hardware into API-controllable devices that agents and software can operate programmatically

- Designing scheduling systems that coordinate dozens of lab instruments with complex dependency chains

You'll own large areas of the product. We're a small team where individual engineers have large impact on what gets built and how.

What we're looking for 

- Full-stack production experience. We use TypeScript, React, Node, Postgres — but what matters is you can work across the stack.

- Product instinct. You've shipped, watched users, iterated, and shipped again.

- Comfortable in ambiguity. You start from a goal, not a spec. You scope problems down, decide what to build and what to skip, and write your own plan when none exists.

- Builds with AI. You use AI tools heavily, but you have enough experience without them to know what good looks like.

- Curious about biology. No background required, but running real experiments in the physical world should excite you.

Application deadline 

We are reviewing applicants on a rolling basis.

title: AI Engineer
description:
Who are we? 

Gain is the Private Markets Super App, a connected global platform transforming how leading investors, advisors, and corporates source, evaluate, and execute deals. By combining investment-grade intelligence, AI-powered workflows, and proprietary data in one unified platform, Gain enables top deal teams to move faster, reduce risk, and build conviction with confidence. 

Gain is trusted across more than $1 trillion of private capital, used by 100% of MBB and Big Four firms, and by 80% of the world’s top 20 M&A advisory houses. 

Recognized for fast innovation and impact, Gain has been named both US and EU Data Provider of the Year by PE Wire, awarded Global Financial Market Review’s Best Use of AI in Finance, and ranked in Sifted’s Top 100 Fastest-Growing Companies, the Forbes 1000, and the Deloitte Technology Fast 50. Gain operates globally with offices in New York, London, Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Warsaw, and Bangalore. 

How we work 

- Predicting what isn't published. Many private companies publish little or no financial detail. Across a database of more than 5 million companies, we predict revenue and EBITDA from sparse labels, and we predict whether and when a company will be bought or sold, which is a time-to-event problem with censored data. 

- Agents on a messy web. Our agents search, navigate and extract company data points from sources that contradict each other, then decide which source to trust before committing to an answer. 

- Quality that holds while everything underneath moves. We're provider-agnostic. Model choices follow the evals, and we switch LLMs when the numbers say so. That only works if the evals are trusted. 

What will you do? 

The work is roughly half LLM agents and half custom ML, leaning slightly toward agents. 

- The design of our agent pipelines: architecture, tools, and which model for which task. You'll shape the technical direction with our AI Lead. 

- The evaluation behind agents and models: offline reference sets, live production evals, and the call on whether an improvement is real. 

- Our prediction models for financials and deals: features, validation, retraining, and knowing when a simpler model wins. 

- Getting work into production: trace where pipelines fail and fix the weakest links first, with compute, memory and model cost in view. 

- Raising the bar in the team through design reviews, pairing, and an eval-first habit that sticks. 

In your first six months you'll own the evals for our agent pipelines, propose where we invest next, and ship measurable improvements to both the agents and the prediction models. 

Who are you? 

- You've built and owned ML systems in production for years, typically 6+ in ML or software engineering. 

- In the last 1–2 years you've shipped LLM agents or pipelines that real users depend on, not demos. 

- You have modelling judgement. You've dealt with leakage, distribution shift and calibration on real data. 

- You measure before you claim. You can build an evaluation set and tell an honest improvement from a lucky one. 

- You care about the user outcome more than the technique. Ideas without a clear customer benefit don't get built here, however interesting. 

- Nice to have: time-to-event modelling, noisy or conflicting data sources, financial or private-company data. No finance background needed. 

The team 

You'll join our Data & AI team of six and report to Renan, our AI Lead who's been building production models for >10 years. Our engineering team runs the infrastructure, and you shape what runs on it. 

The stack 

- Core: Python (async, fully typed with Pydantic) and FastAPI 

- LLMs: multiple providers behind our own provider-agnostic layer, with Pydantic AI for typed agents. 

- Evals and observability: Pydantic Evals and Logfire 

- Data: PostgreSQL with pgvector 

- Cloud: GCP (Cloud Run, Cloud Tasks), Docker, GitHub Actions 

What do we offer? 

- Competitive base salary and annual bonus linked to your performance / OKRs 

- Attractive benefits including health & wellbeing allowance, work-from-home budget, learning & coaching benefits, etc. 

- Flexible hybrid working model with 3 days per week in our Amsterdam office 

- Healthy work-life balance allowing for planability and personal commitments 

- Chance to grow with the company gaining increasing responsibilities, supported by lots of coaching and a feedback-driven approach 

- Tremendous learning and career progression opportunities 

- International environment with hubs in New York, London, Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Warsaw, and Bangalore 

- Culture of trust, ownership and standard of excellence and a fun working atmosphere with regular outings and events 

- Post product-market fit and aspiring unicorn status - this is an excellent time to join & grow with us! 

Does this sound like a perfect match? 

We are proud of our wonderful product and believe it has lots of potential. We are growing fast and having fun while building our platform and company. Does this sound like a team you would like to become a part of? Click ‘Apply’ and submit your CV, we are excited to get to know you and show you what we do!

title: Software Engineer, Lab Automation
description:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. 

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the Role

You'll build work-cell orchestration, instrument drivers, protocol scheduling, error-recovery logic, and monitoring. Physical systems fail in ways pure software doesn't — a plate gets stuck, a liquid handler skips a well, a temperature controller drifts. Your job is to make the system handle all of it gracefully. This is a broad, hands-on role for a strong engineer who wants their code to drive real machines and see it run the same day.

What You'll Do

- Build orchestration software that coordinates liquid handlers, plate readers, incubators, and robot arms — handling timing dependencies, state, and error recovery.

- Reverse-engineer and develop instrument drivers and APIs. Each instrument speaks a different protocol (serial, USB, TCP/IP); you work out how it talks and build a clean abstraction over it.

- Model and execute complex multi-step protocols reliably — a single run can span dozens of steps across multiple instruments.

- Build error-recovery logic so that when something fails mid-run, the system retries, skips, alerts, or pauses depending on the failure mode.

- Create monitoring and observability for work-cell health: instrument status, run progress, error rates.

- Debug across the software–hardware boundary — figuring out whether bad data is a comms, firmware, calibration, or code problem.

- Work closely with lab automation engineers, the rest of the software team, and the scientists running production.

Stack

TypeScript and Python, Postgres (Supabase), Modal for compute. We control instruments with open-source Python tooling like PyLabRobot and PyHamilton wherever we can, rather than proprietary vendor GUIs.

What We're Looking For

- Strong software engineering skills. You write production code in Python and/or TypeScript — well-structured and maintainable, not just prototypes.

- Comfortable at the hardware-software boundary. You've built software that drives physical devices, or you're excited to. You can read a protocol spec, debug a flaky connection, and reason about timing.

- Lab automation experience is a strong plus. Familiarity with PyHamilton, PyLabRobot, Opentrons, or similar tooling helps — as does a background in robotics, industrial automation, IoT, or embedded systems.

- Maker and hacker attitude. You like figuring out how closed systems work and building the thing that makes them work better. Bonus if you're comfortable with electronics, microcontrollers, or a 3D printer when an integration needs a physical fix.

- AI-native builder. It's 2026 — you build with coding agents like Claude Code as a default, and you have sharp judgment about what they produce.

- Self-starter and independent. You define what needs building from how the lab actually works, not just what's in the ticket.

- Reliability-minded. The lab runs 24/7; you design systems where one instrument failing doesn't cascade through the whole work cell.

Biology background not required — but you should be excited that the code runs real experiments.

Details

- Location: Lausanne, Switzerland (on-site — you need hands-on access to physical instruments).

- Type: Full time

- Start date: ASAP

Application deadline 

We are reviewing applicants on a rolling basis.

title: VLA Pre-training & World Models | Humanoid
description:
Role: VLA Pre-training Engineer / Deep Learning Engineer – World Models (2 openings)
Company: Humanoid 
Location: London, UK (King’s Cross) – on-site, five days a week
Job Type: Full-time

About Humanoid 

Humanoid is building the world’s most capable, commercially scalable and safe humanoid robots. Its platform, HMND-01, is already deployed in real industrial environments, which makes Humanoid the most serious humanoid robotics company in Europe.

- 300+ people, 34+ nationalities, flat structure: your decisions ship directly into real robots.

- Offices in London (HQ, King’s Cross), Boston, Vancouver and San Diego.

- Values: Speed, Ambition, Passion, Trust.

About the role 

The VLA Core team builds the base vision-language-action model that the entire manipulation pipeline depends on. This is deep learning at scale: training models from scratch on multi-embodiment trajectory corpora and internet-scale video, with real deployment constraints. The model has to fit and run on a real robot.

Robotics experience is not required. If you come from LLMs, VLMs or video generation, be ready to get up to speed on a new domain quickly.

This is a senior individual contributor role with no management track. The team is research-adjacent, but the output is models that run on robots. Results are shared as blog posts, not papers.

There are two tracks in one team. They are the same role with a different focus, so you can lean into either.

Track 1: VLA Pre-training 

- Pre-train base models on a diverse multi-embodiment corpus of trajectories, fine-tune policies to excel at specific tasks and explore synthetic data.

- Post-train policies with behaviour cloning and RL, and own the full loop from data to deployment.

- Partner with the Data Collection team: specify what good data looks like, identify failure modes, ensure diversity and coverage.

- Run pre-, mid- and post-training on the VLA stack; explore new modalities and architecture changes.

- Build and maintain continuous pipelines: ingest synthetic data and teleop logs, version them, apply weak-supervision labelling, curate balanced datasets and automatically surface fresh failure cases into retraining.

- Work with the MLOps and Data Platform teams to scale distributed training and optimize models for real-time edge inference on the robot.

Track 2: World Models 

- Design and train multimodal, action-conditioned world models (video, state, action and language) using diffusion-based and transformer architectures.

- Build video prediction and dynamics models that stay physically consistent over long horizons, including contact-rich manipulation, and serve as pretrained priors for VLA policies.

- Develop learned-simulator evaluation: score candidate policies offline, predict real-world success rates before deployment, roll out policy futures for safety review and planning.

- Generate synthetic rollouts and counterfactual experience (rare events, cross-platform and sim-to-real transfer) and measure their effect on downstream task performance.

- Build data pipelines that turn fleet telemetry, teleoperation logs and internet-scale video into training corpora.

- Run scaling and ablation studies on architecture, data mixture and context length.

What you need to succeed 

- 3+ years building deep learning systems in industry or research, with shipped models or published work to show for it.

- Deep hands-on experience with at least one of: LLMs, VLMs, image or video generative models (architecture, training and inference). For the World Models track: diffusion models, autoregressive transformers, latent-variable models or video prediction.

- You have actually trained models yourself: pre-training runs, distributed infrastructure, the works. Connecting APIs, building agents or a quick fine-tune is not enough.

- Experience with deep learning infrastructure: streaming datasets, checkpointing and state management, distributed training strategies, debugging numerics and training instabilities.

- Strong Python and PyTorch or JAX. You can profile, optimize data loaders and write maintainable research code.

- Strong coding fundamentals. The process includes a LeetCode-style coding round, so come prepared.

- Empirical rigor: careful evaluations, honest baselines, clear experiment docs, crisp communication of trade-offs.

- You are proactive: you can take an open, messy problem and drive it without waiting for a spec.

- Working English.

Nice to have 

- Robotics or autonomous driving experience; familiarity with simulators (Isaac Sim, MuJoCo) and sim-to-real.

- Experience applying RL to LLMs or robotics.

- Experience with VLA models; familiarity with OpenVLA, Physical Intelligence (π) models or similar open-source frameworks.

- Experience with world models for robotics or autonomous driving (action-conditioned video models, learned simulators, model-based RL).

- Proven productization of deep nets: latency and throughput constraints, on-device optimization, fast inference for generative models.

- Publications at top-tier DL conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CoRL, CVPR) or equivalent open-source contributions.

Interview process 

- Intro call with Igor, hirehire’s AI researcher.

- HR screen with Humanoid.

- Coding round (LeetCode-style).

- Specialization interview (pre-training or world models).

- Technical execution interview: how you work, collaborate and drive problems.

- Optional chat with a tech leader.

What you get 

- Salary: a wide range, set by the level you show in the interviews.

- Equity: stock options with meaningful upside as Humanoid scales.

- 30+ paid days off: 23 days annual leave, all UK bank holidays and a company shutdown between Christmas and New Year.

- Private healthcare: fully funded, including virtual and in-person care.

- Pension: 8% total contribution (5% employee, 3% employer) on full earnings.

- Daily food: free breakfast, catered lunch and snacks in the office.

- Real ownership: direct access to founding leadership, real input on product direction and room to drive key initiatives from day one.

- Visa sponsorship and relocation to London.

title: Software Engineer
description:
Who are we? 

At UpGuard , we are replacing manual security bottlenecks with AI-driven precision. Fresh off a US$75M Series C, we are scaling our infrastructure to process 100 billion risk signals daily. This isn’t just growth; it’s a total reimagining of how the world manages cyber risk.

We build the Cyber Risk Posture Management (CRPM) platform that security teams actually love. By integrating security ratings, threat intel, and agentic AI, we empower organisations to stay ahead of an ever evolving attack surface.

We aren’t just building another tool; we’re defining a category. We provide the autonomy to ship world-class technology and the resources to do it at a global scale.

About the role 

We're hiring a Software Engineer to join our Product Engineering team. You'll work across the whole stack: customer-facing features in React and TypeScript, Go services that process security data at internet scale, and the plumbing that keeps it all secure and reliable. You'll ship real work in your first weeks with a senior engineer as your buddy, and your scope will grow as you're ready for it. You don't need to know cybersecurity yet, but you do need to be curious about it.

You'll join one of our 11 (and growing) Product Engineering squads, most of which have a product manager, designer and technical lead alongside the engineers.

Our stack is React and TypeScript on the front end, Go services with Postgres as our primary database, running on Kubernetes via Google Cloud Platform.

Our engineers work with agentic coding tools, mostly Claude Code and Cursor, and a growing part of the product is LLM-backed. You'll work this way from day one, and we'll want your ideas on what to automate next, from how we write code to how we test, review, ship and run it.

Own well-scoped work end to end, with senior engineers to pair with and review your designs

Help keep the platform fast and reliable as we scale

Grow toward senior, with increasing scope as you're ready and a manager focused on getting you there

What we're looking for 

- 
Typically 2+ years of relevant engineering experience

Strong TypeScript and React

Solid relational database skills (we use Postgres)

AI coding tools as your default workflow, and the judgment to review and own what they produce
